Lab 8 progress write-up: 30–31 October 2026

Astro 331 Lab 8, 3-DOF reaction-wheel air-bearing table (Gowri Ramaprasad, Derek Weissinger, Owen Crawley). Covers the work of 30 and 31 October: what was built, how it was tested, what the simulations predicted, what the table actually did, and what is left. Figures come from the SD logs in test_runs/; the script that makes them is Reports/figures/writeup_2026-10-31/make_figs.py. Day-by-day detail is in PROGRESS_LOG.md §2.15–2.25.

1. Summary

Over these two days the table went from "controller written and simulated, not run" to running every requirement test closed-loop on the air bearing:

  • Requirement 1 (hold a heading): STEP TEST on the air bearing. ±5° heading steps rise in 1.2–1.7 s, settle in 1.6–2.0 s with ≤ 4% overshoot, and hold with ≤ 0.03° rms jitter. The yaw inertia was measured for the first time: Izz = 0.0759 / 0.0776 kg·m², against 0.0623 in the model.
  • Requirement 2 (attitude to ±1°): two real errors in the heading were found and fixed:
    • a magnetic field fixed to the table, 2.4× Earth's horizontal field, which made the magnetometer aid pull the estimate up to 9°;
    • a 0.9% yaw gyro scale error, about 3.5° per full turn.
    After both fixes, a 360° slew sequence ends dead on the tape marker by eye. A measured truth (laser) is still missing.
  • Requirement 3 (wheel failure): FAULT TEST passed on the table. Wheel B was made dead mid-hold, detected in 0.91 s, and attitude never left ±1° (peak 0.79° yaw). Fourteen false "dead motor" alarms from static friction were diagnosed and fixed.
  • Stretch (4-attitude slew): tilted targets are physically impossible on this pendulous table. Measured cost: ~11 mN·m of wheel torque per degree away from the rest tilt. The new SLEW YAW (four headings with roll and pitch left at the rest tilt) passed 4/4 on the table four times, ending on the marker with the final firmware.
  • Hardware and data:
    • the table is balanced to roll −0.9°, pitch −0.7° at rest;
    • the wheel speed limit was raised 60 → 80 rad/s after a vibration check;
    • IMU sample gaps were traced to SD-card writes;
    • wheel D has an intermittent fault that is not yet found;
    • the room at the presentation spot distorts the magnetic field, so the magnetometer aid is now off by default.

2. Starting point (morning of 30 October)

  • Firmware already in place:
    • multiplicative EKF (gyro + accelerometer, plus a gated heading-only magnetometer aid since 10-27);
    • quaternion PD attitude controller with a pyramid allocation over any 3 or 4 wheels;
    • DEMO LEVEL (hold the heading and only damp roll/pitch at the table's natural rest tilt);
    • first drafts of SLEW TEST and FAULT TEST, simulated but never run on the table.
  • The Teensy had just been replaced (the old board's 3.3 V rail shorted; Reports/Teensy_Recovery_2026-10-30.html). The spare's VIN and VUSB pads are still joined, so since then every upload is done over USB with both switches off, and the table is run on battery over the XBee only.
  • The table is pendulous: its centre of mass sits below the bearing centre, so gravity pulls it back to a rest tilt and any held tilt costs steady wheel torque (§2.7 of the progress log). That fact shapes most of what follows.

3. 30 October: MAG TEST and the tools for the table

3.1 MAG TEST: validating the magnetometer yaw aid (to-do item 6)

MAG TEST [min] is a scripted, fixed-table validation of the magnetometer aid with all four wheels. The table is clamped, so any yaw the estimator reports is error. The script has 22 steps:

  • wheels stopped, then the wheels in 11 direction patterns at 200 rpm (first visits learn references);
  • repeats at 100/300 rpm and mixed speeds;
  • three ±10° "kicks" of the estimate to test recovery;
  • then a 30-min drift run cycling 2-min steps.

Each step passes if |yaw| ≤ 1°. Kick steps pass if the estimate is back within 1° within 90 s.

Run 1 (MAGTEST_0001, after a 10-min warm-up and CALIBRATE 180):

  • 36/37 steps passed on board. The one miss was 1.02° (all wheels at 300 rpm, a pattern first learned at 200 rpm).
  • Kicks recovered in 73–84 s. The aid was in use 92% of the time, and the drift-run trend was −0.40 °/h.
  • The same data replayed gyro-only drifts 5.7 °/h: it would leave ±1° after about 12 minutes (Fig. 1).

3.2 Heading-hold wheel bias (null_bias.h)

Stopped or slowly reversing motor shafts leave a random magnetometer offset and gate the aid. The four-wheel pyramid has a null mode [+1, −1, +1, −1] that produces no body torque. A planner now sets that null mode every step during ARM and DEMO LEVEL so that every wheel stays at least 100 rpm from zero, at the lowest possible peak speed, capped at 45 rad/s (now 65). When the stored momentum would push a wheel through zero, it jumps to the next direction pattern through the null mode, in about 1 s with no body torque.

Motor-level simulation, pendulous DEMO LEVEL for 420 s:

  • no wheel spent more than 0.4 s below 4 rad/s, against 115 s without the planner;
  • 2 pattern changes;
  • yaw error 0.06°;
  • same hold length as without it, and no false dead-motor alarms.

On the table it chattered (§4.2), which was fixed on 10-31.

3.3 Tools and firmware built the same day

  • Runtime tuning (SET/GET, tune.h): gains, inertias, speed-loop gains, magnetometer parameters, IMU mount angles, and more. Tried over the XBee without an upload, and reset at reboot.
  • STEP TEST: requirement-1 tuning on the air bearing.
    • Sequence: DEMO LEVEL, then hold, then +5°, 0, −5°, 0 heading steps, 20 s each, with rise, overshoot, settle, error and jitter reported per step.
    • Yaw inertia: Izz comes from momentum exchange, fitting I(ψ−ψ0) + ∫(hz−hz0)dt = τdragt²/2 over 6 s after each step. Gravity has no yaw torque, so this works even on the pendulous table.
    • Simulation: the first version differentiated the encoder speeds and was biased by their filter lag. The integrated form recovered Izz within 3% in the motor-level simulation.
  • LEVEL ZERO: averages the accelerometer for 5 s with the deck physically level and stores the IMU's mounting rotation, so the reported attitude is the table's, not the IMU board's.
  • Log replay (tools/replay): runs an SD log through the firmware's own attitude_ekf.cpp and mag_aid.cpp on the PC in seconds, with options (gyro-only, prediction on/off, hard iron, noise values). It reproduced MAGTEST_0001's on-board yaw to 0.047° rms, which makes it a trustworthy "what if" tool. It was used for most of the analysis below.
  • Report and fitting tools:
    • tools/magtest_report.py: HTML report of a MAG TEST;
    • tools/hardiron_fit.py: table hard iron from a yaw turn;
    • tools/balance.py: centre of mass from free swings.
  • Replay finding: run 1's miss came from learning each new pattern's reference at whatever yaw error existed at that moment. Predicting new references from a known one passed 37/37 in replay, so prediction was made the default and uploaded on 10-31.

4. 31 October: MAG TEST rerun and heading holds

4.1 MAG TEST run 2: prediction failed, reverted

With prediction on board, MAGTEST_0002 stopped at step 15 with 10/15 passing. The fails were 1.02–1.21°, all on first visits to new wheel patterns. The reversal model the prediction relied on had moved by about 1° between sessions, and the raw field strength had changed (71.1 → 64.7 µT), so the magnetic surroundings were different. Replays of both runs under every variant showed that each new pattern costs 0.3–1.2° of reference error either way: that is the floor of this magnetometer placement. The team can't move the IMU, so the firmware went back to learning new patterns in place, and holds keep pattern changes to one or two.

Same day: the SD logger was rewritten to write whole, sector-aligned blocks up to 8 KB from a 96 KB buffer. Both MAG TESTs had lost rows in multi-minute bursts. Afterwards: 0 rows lost over 9 min.

4.2 DEMO LEVEL heading holds on the air bearing (DEMO_0003)

  • Aid on, 214 s: the estimate held ±0.2° (controller error 0.02° rms).
  • Aid off, 189 s: similar.
  • Truth: an independent magnetometer heading moved ≤ 0.5°, and the heading held by eye at the tape marker.
  • Planner chatter: the wheel-bias planner flipped between two patterns 15 times in 6 s. The candidates were near-tied, and a wheel stuck near zero by static friction tipped the choice each time. The simulation had no static friction and didn't show this.
  • Fix: decide on 0.5 s low-passed speeds, treat clearances within 1 rad/s as equal, and keep each choice for at least 5 s. Replaying the run gives 1 change.

5. Balancing the table

New permanent weight holders had shifted the centre of mass (CG), so the table was rebalanced iteratively. Each reading used tools/rest_tilt.py over the XBee:

  • BIAS 0, then DEMO LEVEL (heading held, roll/pitch only damped), wait for "settled", hold, STOP.
  • That gives the rest tilt without the table spinning.
  • tools/balance_live.py fits the free swing for the CG height.

Fig. 2 shows every reading.

  • Measurement problems found and fixed:
    • The IMU mount could rock, causing ~10° jumps between readings. It was glued, then LEVEL ZERO was done with a phone level. It was redone 1.5 h later because the glue crept 1.1° in pitch (now 3.611° / −2.164°).
    • Repeat readings scatter ~0.3°. Another ~0.3° turns with heading (a torque fixed to the room, likely the bearing air flow). Readings at one fixed heading (tape markers, wheel C at the tape) agree within ~0.15°.
    • Axis check: moves along y seemed not to change roll. A wheel-A kick on the floating table produced 2.51° of roll swing and 0.37° of pitch, which proved the IMU axes match the wheel layout. The earlier move estimates were simply unreliable.
  • Removing the loose heavy weights and the top screws lowered the CG from ~5.7 to ~13 mm below the bearing centre (swing 4.3 → 2.9 s). The table became twice as stiff: ~1,150 g·mm of trim per degree, so a battery pack re-seated 3 mm off now moves it only ~0.4°.
  • Final trim: 3 × 8 g washers on each of the CD and AD seats (55 mm out). That predicted +2.3° of roll, and it moved +2.3°. Final rest tilt ≈ −0.9° roll, −0.7° pitch.
  • Decision: stop fine balancing.
    • Requirements 1–3 all run at the rest tilt, so they don't need it.
    • Tilted slews would need the CG within ~0.02 mm. That's impossible by hand when packs are re-velcroed at every charge.
    • Rule from here: re-trim only if the rest tilt exceeds ±5°.

6. Wheels: false alarms, wheel D, speed limit, IMU gaps

6.1 False "dead motor" alarms from static friction

The dead-motor detector flags a wheel that is driven with effort (duty − speed/160) ≥ 0.2 but gains less than 25% of the predicted speed for 0.2 s. DEMO_0004/0005 contained 14 such flags (13 on wheel D, 1 on A). Every one was a wheel at rest whose speed loop wound the duty up to 0.23–0.30 without the wheel moving. Healthy starts break free at 0.10–0.15 duty, occasionally up to 0.27 (Fig. 3).

Fix: a wheel at standstill now counts as dead only at effort ≥ 0.4, just under the current-limit cap of 0.45. A dead motor still trips once the loop winds up, and spinning-wheel detection (FAULT TEST) is unchanged. Replaying both logs through the new rule gives 0 flags. The encoder-fault check had the same weakness (duty > 0.2 with no motion for 0.5 s) and was raised to 0.4 for the same reason. Since then: 4 + 4 DEMO LEVEL starts and several test runs with no false flags.

6.2 Wheel D: weak, then healthy, then a real failure

  • Morning: open-loop TEST D 0.3 reached 33–36 rad/s against 46–47 for A–C, with all packs at 12.0 V.
  • After the pack-voltage check and a power cycle: the encoder was exact (10 hand turns = 4,002 counts), there was no drag by hand, and D spun normally (45.6–46.8 rad/s both ways).
  • DEMO_0008, the evening session: D did not turn at all on three Armed starts while its duty went to the 0.45 limit (Fig. 8). Those flags were correct, and wheels A and C absorbed D's share. That is why the first SLEW YAW stopped on the wheel limit.
  • After a wiring check and another power cycle: normal again through 4 DEMO LEVEL starts and two full SLEW YAWs.

Two explanations fit, and the data can't separate them: a poor connection in D's power path that touching or vibration opens and closes, or driver D latching off on over-current (its fault pin isn't wired, so the firmware can't see it).

6.3 Wheel speed limit 60 → 80 rad/s, and vibration

The accelerating torque left at wheel speed ω is min(0.45, 0.95 − ω/160) of stall torque. That is full torque up to ~79 rad/s on a 12 V pack, 85% at 90 and 71% at 100. The limit was raised to 80 rad/s, with the related limits moved with it: overspeed trip 90, demo/slew abort 75, hold-bias peak 65. This gives one third more momentum capacity. A clamped run at ±760 rpm showed little vibration: accelerometer standard deviation ≤ 0.10 m/s² against 0.02 at rest, with the gyro unaffected (Fig. 4, left).

6.4 IMU sample gaps are SD-card writes

The same log showed gyro gaps of 60–130 ms (5–12 samples) in pairs about 0.27 s apart, every ~1.67 MB of log (~53 s), whether the wheels were stopped or spinning (Fig. 4, right). The spacing follows the bytes written more closely than time, so it comes from the SD write path, not vibration. Gaps over the old 100 ms IMU timeout were dropped by the EKF, so the rotation during them was lost: ~0.75° at slew rates. The timeout is now 300 ms so they are integrated. The root cause in the SD path is still open.

7. Requirements 1 and 3 on the air bearing (DEMO_0007, DEMO_0008)

7.1 STEP TEST (requirement 1)

First run (DEMO_0007, warm board, CALIBRATE 180, wheel bias on):

  • ±5° steps: rise 1.52–1.56 s, 0% overshoot, settle 1.79–1.90 s;
  • final error ≤ 0.12°, jitter ≤ 0.04° rms;
  • measured Izz = 0.0776 kg·m², with yaw drag ≤ 0.07 mN·m.

The controller held its estimate perfectly, but the table ended visibly off the tape marker; §8 explains why. After the fixes, the rerun (DEMO_0008, Fig. 6) had:

  • rise 1.22–1.66 s, overshoot 1–4%, settle 1.57–1.96 s;
  • final error ≤ 0.003°, jitter ≤ 0.03° rms;
  • Izz = 0.0759;
  • back on the marker by eye.

Izz = 0.0768 (the mean) is now the firmware default.

7.2 FAULT TEST (requirement 3)

FAULT TEST B 10 on DEMO LEVEL: after 10 s of holding, wheel B's motor was held at zero current without telling the controller. Results:

  • Detection: 0.91 s; wheel B was taken out of service and coasted.
  • Recovery: back within ±1° 0.9 s after the failure.
  • Errors: peak 0.01° roll, 0.02° pitch, 0.79° yaw; 30-s hold maximum 0.70° yaw.
  • Grade: PASS (Fig. 7).

The detection margin is thin (0.91 s against a 1 s limit; the simulation gave 0.6–0.8 s), and only wheel B has been tested.

8. Heading truth: hard iron and gyro scale

8.1 The table's own magnetic field (hard iron)

Replaying DEMO_0007 gyro-only showed what the table really did in the first STEP TEST (Fig. 5, left). It turned +5.9 → +7.4° for the +5° step and sat +2.7° off the start at the first return to 0, which is what was seen at the marker. Meanwhile the estimate said ±0.1°. The magnetometer aid had pulled the estimate by 2.9° in that test, and by up to 8.6° while the table was turned by hand.

The cause: a circle fit of the horizontal field over a 376° free turn (wheels stopped, aid off) gives Earth's horizontal field as 22.4 µT and a field fixed to the table of (+20.5, −48.9) µT, from the motors, batteries and steel. That is 2.4× Earth's. Fixed-table MAG TESTs can't see it, so it had never been calibrated. With it removed (now kMagHardIronUt), the replayed pull drops to 0.7° in the step test and 0.9° in the hand turns.

8.2 Yaw gyro scale factor

The first SLEW YAW that ran on four wheels (DEMO_0009) passed 4/4 but ended a few degrees past the marker after 360° of slews. In that run the aid was idle and the z bias constant, so the estimate was pure gyro: the gyro itself under-reads. Comparing the integrated gyro with the magnetometer's absolute heading over two free turns in DEMO_0007 gives true/gyro = 1.0090 and 1.0085 (Fig. 12).

A hand test against the tape marker (3 turns each way) agreed in direction (2–3% short), but each leg had several degrees of alignment and air-bearing creep uncertainty. The firmware now multiplies every yaw gyro sample by kGyroScaleZ = 1.009 (SET GYRO_SZ to adjust). With it, the next run ended slightly short with the magnetometer aid on at the new spot, and dead on the marker gyro-only (§10). So the true value is about 1.006–1.009.

9. Stretch requirement: SLEW TEST to SLEW YAW

The required slew visits four attitudes along the shortest path, reaching each within ±1° in all three axes. The default targets include 8–10° tilts. On this table, each degree away from the rest tilt costs ~11 mN·m of steady wheel torque. The wheels can absorb ~0.035 N·m·s about a tilt axis, so a 10° tilt fills them in about 0.3 s.

Even with yaw-only targets and roll/pitch fixed at the measured rest tilt (−1.2°, −0.2°), SLEW TEST stopped on the wheel limit 13.5 s into the first slew (Fig. 9, left). Wheels A and C filled in opposite directions, which is roll momentum: at that heading the table wanted ~−1.5° roll, and 0.3° of mismatch costs ~3 mN·m.

SLEW YAW (new) is the stretch test as this table can do it:

  • the same four targets, using only their headings (+45°, +135°, −135°, 0° from the start);
  • yaw follows the same smooth eigenaxis slew profile (cosine, peak 0.1 rad/s and 0.02 rad/s²);
  • the roll/pitch reference is the measured tilt every step, so those axes are only damped, as in DEMO LEVEL;
  • graded like SLEW TEST: within ±1° for 1 s to count as reached, then 5 s held within ±1°, with roll/pitch measured from the rest tilt.

Rotation about the vertical is the shortest path between attitudes that differ only in heading. Table runs:

DEMO_0009after D's wiring check4/4 PASS0.04–0.05 / 0.12–0.17 / 0.06–0.08°a few degrees past (gyro scale)

10. The presentation spot

The table was moved to where it will be presented. There the field is bent by nearby steel:

  • Earth's horizontal component is only 15.4–15.8 µT (22.4 µT at the first spot).
  • The magnetometer heading error that depends on heading is 4.1° peak-to-peak with the wheels stopped, against 1.8° at the first spot, with the circle centre fitted freely (Fig. 11, left).
  • Moving all metal at least 1.5 m away helped only partly; the rest is fixed structure.

A room-distortion correction was written: a one- and two-per-turn Fourier correction of the field direction (SET MAG_C1/S1/C2/S2, fitted with tools/mag_room_fit.py). Calibration turns were run with the wheels spinning (±100 rpm, zero net momentum), because stopped motor shafts add a ~5 µT offset that changes every time the wheels stop. Fits with the wheels stopped came out with completely different coefficients. With the firmware's hard iron and wheel model applied and 0.5 s smoothing:

  • Uncorrected: 14.3° peak-to-peak.
  • Corrected, fit and test on the same data: 1.7°.
  • Corrected, fit on one turn direction and tested on the other: 3.5° and 5.3° (Fig. 11, right).

That leaves ±2–2.5° of heading error from the magnetometer. A warm-calibrated, scale-corrected gyro drifts ~3 °/h, under 0.2° over a demo.

Decision: the magnetometer aid is now off at boot (kMagAidDefaultOn = false; MAG ON re-enables it). The correction code is uploaded with its coefficients at 0. The final SLEW YAW (SLEW_0002) ran this way and ended dead on the marker.

11. Simulation methods, and simulation vs the table

11.1 Methods

  1. Motor-level Python simulation (Reports/Slew_and_Fault_Simulation.html, built 10-29, extended 10-30):
    • Truth model: a separate rigid-body model of the table (I = 0.08 kg·m², pendulum swing period 3.3 s ≈ 5 mN·m/deg, measured yaw drag 0.12 mN·m).
    • Firmware copies, run at 100 Hz: speed filter, PI speed loop, current limit, duty cap and slew limit, allocation and null mode, attitude controller, encoder-fault check, dead-motor detector, FAULT TEST, SLEW TEST, the DEMO LEVEL rest-tilt reference, and (10-30) the wheel-bias planner and STEP TEST.
    • Motors: torque = stall torque × (duty − speed/free speed), with per-pack free speeds 150–166 rad/s, Coulomb friction (4–6 mN·m) plus viscous drag, wheel J +12% for the motor rotor, and encoder quantisation at 400 counts/turn.
    • Attitude: truth plus gyro noise.
  2. Host C++ slew simulation (tools/slewsim, 10-31): the firmware's actual slew_test.cpp, attitude_ctrl.cpp, tune.cpp and allocation, compiled on the PC.
    • Table: pendulous rigid body (I = 0.14/0.14/0.0776 kg·m², 5.1 kg, CG 13 mm low with a small horizontal offset).
    • Disturbances: a room-fixed torque (0–4 mN·m, so the rest tilt moves with heading) and yaw drag.
    • Simplifications: ideal wheel torques (no motor or speed-loop model) and a perfect estimate.
    • Use: design SLEW YAW and check it against the old fixed-tilt SLEW TEST before uploading.
  3. Offline replays of recorded logs: the estimator replay (tools/replay, the firmware's EKF and aid on logged sensor data) and a detector replay (old vs new dead-motor rule on DEMO_0004/0005). These aren't models; they test changed firmware on real data. The replay reproduced on-board yaw to 0.047° rms, which is why its conclusions were trusted.

Overall: the simulations predicted the architecture-level results correctly. Detection works, 3-wheel control recovers, tilted slews are impossible on a pendulous table, yaw-only slews work, and the STEP TEST inertia estimator works. They missed the hardware details: static friction, intermittent wiring, the table's magnetic field, the gyro scale and the room. Every one of those was found by flying the table and checking it against a reference.

13. Next steps

  1. Measured heading truth (requirement 2): mount a laser pointer on the deck aimed at a far wall, mark the dot, and:
    • run SLEW YAW and measure the dot's offset at the end;
    • do 3 hand turns each way, at about 10 m from the wall, to resolve the gyro scale to ~0.1% (SET GYRO_SZ);
    • do a 10-min DEMO LEVEL hold and track the dot (requirement 1).
    For roll/pitch, check the estimate against the phone level on the deck at rest. Also re-check LEVEL ZERO once the glue has fully cured.
  2. Requirement 3 coverage: run FAULT TEST A, C, D and one FAULT TEST REAL (pull a motor lead). Because detection took 0.91 s against a 1 s limit, consider shortening the detector's confirmation time if any wheel comes in over.
  3. Wheel D: solder or crimp its power and encoder connections with strain relief. If it drops out again: spin-test it before touching anything, then cycle only the motor switch to test the driver-latch theory. Wiring the drivers' fault pin to a spare Teensy pin would make latch-offs visible.
  4. Wheel bias with the aid off: the bias exists for the magnetometer. With the aid off, compare BIAS 0 against the default in SLEW YAW and holds. It may remove the 0.2–0.5° pattern-change transients, but wheels would then pass through zero (static friction).
  5. Presentation procedure (each session):
    1. Power on, warm up 5 min.
    2. Clamp, CALIBRATE 180.
    3. Float at the marker.
    4. STEP TEST, SLEW YAW, FAULT TEST.
    Spin-test the wheels (TEST x 0.3, all ≈ 46 rad/s) before the session.
  6. Housekeeping:
    • commit today's firmware, tools and logs;
    • update the final deck (tomorrow; the MAG TEST slides still describe the prediction replay);
    • find the SD-write stall;
    • measure Ixx/Iyy (swing fits suggest ~0.14 kg·m²);
    • model the motor rotor momentum.

    • commands MAG TEST, STEP TEST, LEVEL ZERO, SET/GET;
    • heading-hold wheel bias (BIAS);
    • predicted references (later reverted).
  • 31 Oct:
    • SD logger (sector-aligned, 96 KB buffer);
    • wheel-bias planner chatter fix;
    • dead-motor and encoder-check standstill thresholds 0.4;
    • speed limit 80 rad/s;
    • IMU gap limit 300 ms;
    • IMU mount 3.611/−2.164°;
    • hard iron (+20.5, −48.9, 0) µT;
    • SLEW YAW;
    • Izz 0.0768;
    • yaw gyro scale 1.009;
    • room correction (0);
    • aid off at boot.

Tools

  • tools/replay: estimator replay; options --nomag, --hard, --room, and others.
  • tools/slewsim: SLEW TEST / SLEW YAW host simulation, with optional trace CSV.
  • tools/magtest_report.py: MAG TEST report.
  • tools/hardiron_fit.py, tools/mag_room_fit.py: magnetometer calibration.
  • tools/balance.py, tools/balance_live.py, tools/rest_tilt.py: balance measurements.

Logs used here (test_runs/)

  • MAGTEST_0001/0002: the two MAG TEST runs.
  • DEMO_0003: DEMO LEVEL holds, aid on and off.
  • DEMO_0004/0005: balance session and false alarms.
  • STATIC_0008 31 Oct: vibration check and IMU gaps.
  • DEMO_0007: STEP TEST, FAULT TEST and fixed-tilt SLEW TEST.
  • DEMO_0008: STEP TEST rerun, wheel D failure, first SLEW YAW.
  • DEMO_0009: SLEW YAW with the gyro-scale overshoot.
  • SLEW_0001: presentation spot runs, hand turns and calibration turns.
  • SLEW_0002: final SLEW YAW.
  • balance_iterations_2026-10-31.txt: every balance reading with notes.
